summary: In a major national security development, U.S. Air Force and Space Force officials announced that the military operates deployed space control weapons in orbit to bolster deterrence against prospective threats. The revelation comes as defense leaders warn a budget impasse imperils 10 percent of Space Force programs, even as the service establishes a new space technology portfolio executive and plans to add 10,000 guardians over the next five years. Concurrently, the U.S. State Department launched a new space-diplomacy initiative to support global partner engagement. In civil space and science, NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope captured a dynamic panorama of star formation revealing the smallest known brown dwarfs, while the Roman Space Telescope doubled its operational lifetime following a super-precise engine burn. On the human exploration front, the Artemis III astronaut crew visited Kennedy Space Center’s Vehicle Assembly Building as NASA prepares for International Observe the Moon Night on Sept. 19. In commercial launch activity, SpaceX is slated to launch its second classified mission for the Space Force tonight, reflecting broader market trends forecasting a fourfold increase in space-based intelligence launches over the next decade. Looking ahead, industry observers should watch for SpaceX’s next Starship launch scheduled for Sept. 22, which aims to reach orbit for the first time.
